lane: Mobile: iOS Lô 1, code and configuration readiness for an iOS build (no Apple account, no store setting, no sale)
goal: Prepare the shared Expo app so an iOS build can be produced next to Android: iOS fields in app.json, an account-free simulator build profile in eas.json, a per-platform public key for the in-app purchase SDK (Android key and a new iOS key; iOS stays off until the Owner sets the key), the purchase SDK allowed to load on iOS, and release-config checks for the iOS fields.
successCriteria: app.json ios has the same bundle id as the Android package, the shared build number, usesNonExemptEncryption=false and supportsTablet=false (iPhone only for the first App Store release).
eas.json has a preview-simulator profile (iOS simulator build, internal) so native iOS compile can be checked on EAS without Apple credentials.
billingPublicKeyForPlatform returns the Android key on android, the iOS key on ios and undefined elsewhere; purchases stay unavailable on iOS while EXPO_PUBLIC_REVENUECAT_IOS_KEY is empty.
loadPurchasesModule is allowed on ios as well as android when the native module exists; web and Expo Go still get no purchases.
validate-mobile-release-config fails when iOS bundle id differs from the Android package or usesNonExemptEncryption is not false.
tsc, mobile jest suite and mobile release-config validation pass.
untouchedSurfaces: No backend, SQL, Edge Function, Admin, RevenueCat dashboard, App Store Connect or Apple account change.
premiumOnSale stays false; no purchase screen becomes visible because of this change.
No new package; no generated ios/ folder (the iOS project stays generated by EAS).
Android behaviour, key name EXPO_PUBLIC_REVENUECAT_ANDROID_KEY and versionCode stay unchanged.

impact.entryPoint: EAS iOS build, app.json iOS section, billing client creation at app start.
impact.dataWrite: No data is written; configuration and client code only.
impact.backendContract: None changed; the shared premium entitlement and webhook are untouched.
impact.privacySafety: No new data collected or sent; the iOS public key is a client key, never a secret.
